newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares settle with gains, seen uptrending.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares settle with gains, seen uptrending.

text.p: Greek shares followed up on Friday's strong rebound settling with moderate gains after trading higher early in the session. Market watchers saw more room for an advance up to a first resistance level of 970-980 points.

"I expect the benchmark share index to close the year at quite higher levels. It's clear that the 40 basis point cut in the 12-month T-bill rate to 12.3 percent has benefited the market. It will likely spark a new round of interest rate cuts this week which will lead real savings rate to 1.0 percent," said analyst Emmanuel Varsos at Investment Analysis.
National Bank of Greece said on Friday it will trim its savings deposit rate by 25 basis points down to 11.25 percent effective November 4.
"On the inflation front, if the October CPI figure improves by at least a tenth of a point to below 8.4 percent, market sentiment will improve," he said.
Moreover, the finalisation of the much talked about government plan to tax interest earned on state debt paper has not been discounted by the equities market he added.

Friday's upside reaction came amid expectations that the government is planning to tax interest earned on T-bills, derivatives such as swaps, options and FRAs and revamp the tax status of mutual funds as the market awaits the 1997 budget.
The finance ministry cut 40 basis point cut in the marker 12-month T-bill, down to 12.30 percent. The issue came to market on Thursday and sold very well.
The Athens general share index closed up 0.42 percent or 3.95 points higher at 942.16 from Friday's 938.21 close. Turnover rose to 8.2 billion drachmas on volume of 4.8 million shares.
